article.articleHeadline: UGM expert reveals symptoms and ways to prevent Influenza A, whose cases are surging again in Indonesia
article.articleSummary:
- Influenza A cases are surging in Indonesia. Ministry of Health data through September 12, 2026 show influenza positivity at 38% in week 35, up from 22% the prior week. Of 175 specimens tested, 66 were positive, with most identified as influenza A(H1N1)pdm09. UGM microbiology professor Tri Wibawa notes the rise should not cause undue panic, but warrants risk mitigation. Typical symptoms include fever (sometimes with chills), cough, sore throat, runny or congested nose, muscle/body aches, headache, and fatigue. High-risk groups are older adults (≥65), children under 5, people with chronic diseases, and those with weakened immune systems. Prevention emphasizes healthy living, hand hygiene, proper cough/sneeze etiquette, mask use when ill, and vaccination, especially for high-risk individuals.

High-risk groups for complications include those over 65, children under five, people with chronic diseases, and the immunocompromised. To reduce transmission, several simple preventive steps are advised. Reporting from Liputan6.com in Jakarta.

article.articleHeadline: Colorimetric LAMP Test Matches PCR for Rapid Mpox Detection in Clinical
article.articleSummary: Mpox, now globally relevant since the 2022 multi-country outbreak, reported 52,845 confirmed cases and 215 deaths in 2025 across 98 countries, with ongoing transmission especially in several African nations. Indian researchers at ICMR-NIV Pune clinically validated a colorimetric LAMP assay for mpox diagnosis suitable for laboratories with limited infrastructure. The dual-target test uses orthopoxvirus B6R (genus-specific) and mpox F3L (species-specific) genes, plus an internal human beta-actin control; a specimen is mpox-positive only if both targets are positive. Readout is via a pH-sensitive dye that turns pink to yellow on amplification, allowing visual interpretation. In a clinical evaluation of 130 specimens (50 mpox-positive, 80 mpox-negative by qPCR) spanning nasopharyngeal and throat swabs, vesicle swabs, lesion swabs, crust specimens, and lesion fluid specimens, the results were striking, highlighting a rapid, accessible alternative to qPCR.

article.articleHeadline: Robotic surgery at SGPGI ends 6 yrs of agony caused by rare TB complication
article.articleSummary: Tubercular vesicovaginal fistula (TVF), a rare genital TB complication, caused continuous urinary leakage in a 20-year-old girl from Lucknow. Six months of anti-tubercular therapy (Sept 2025–Feb 2026) followed by a three-month break culminated in a May 2026 robotic repair at SGPGI, led by Prof Sanjay Surekha with Dr Apran Yadav, aided by 3D visualization to dissect dense scar tissue, close the fistula, and rebuild the bladder. The operation yielded minimal blood loss and quick recovery. At a Sept 2026 post-op follow-up, she was pain-free, had gained weight, and planned to resume studies. The team acknowledged Prof MS Ansari, anaesthetist Dr Tapas Singh, and resident doctors for the success.

Sterilization plus vaccination are urged; Taiwan’s New Taipei City shows that maintaining female sterilization above 70% reduced outdoor dogs by about half over seven years and cut puppy admissions by 88%, while Cheung Chau studies were inconclusive. Practical safety: dismount, use bike as barrier, face dogs and back away slowly; night travel in groups with bright lights.

article.articleHeadline: Is Dengue Fever No Longer Exclusive to the South? Beijing's Local Risk Is Low, but Travelers Should Take Mosquito Precautions.
article.articleSummary: Beijing currently has low local risk for dengue fever, but imported cases sustain potential transmission. As of August 2026, Beijing reported 14 dengue cases, all imported from overseas. Dengue fever, chikungunya fever, and Zika virus disease are mosquitoborne concerns; the main Beijing vector is Aedes albopictus, not a major driver of local outbreaks. Nevertheless, importation can spark secondary cases via travel with dengue-affected countries. Risk areas for residents include: National Day trips to southern China when vector density peaks; travel to Southeast Asia (Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia); and outdoor time in Beijing parks, where Aedes albopictus bites at dawn and dusk. Prevention emphasizes outdoor wear (long sleeves, light colors), repellents with DEET, picaridin, or IR3535; interior measures include intact screens and removing standing water. If after travel fever with headaches, eye/joint pains, or redness on face/neck/chest occurs, seek medical advice and report travel history.

article.articleHeadline: Scientists' alarm: the world is unprepared for a new pandemic.
article.articleSummary: Nus-Lancet Prime Commission warns the world is unprepared for a new pandemic. COVID-19 caused more than 7 million confirmed deaths and an estimated 28 million excess deaths, exposing major gaps in health security and social, economic, and governance systems. Nearly seven years after the first infections in China, the global risk of another pandemic remains, despite repeated WHO warnings that it will happen, not if. The Commission’s Pandemic Readiness through Institutions, Mobilising Communities and Equity framework calls for moving beyond traditional technical preparedness to a broader readiness that includes social protection, financing, regulatory standards, education, labor policies, food systems, and environmental governance. Modeling a hypothetical influenza A outbreak shows that equitable vaccine distribution could cut global mortality by about 64% to 21.2 million deaths, saving ~37.3 million lives. The report notes revised International Health Regulations and debates on the WHO Pandemic Accord, with UN high-level meetings looming but concrete commitments seen as lacking.

article.articleHeadline: Gut Parasites in Captive Macaques Reveal Close Genetic Ties to Human
article.articleSummary: Entamoeba parasites in captive crab-eating macaques (Macaca fascicularis) from commercial breeding farms in Beijing and Suzhou, China, show high prevalence of E. coli (49.0%), E. dispar (36.5%), and notable E. histolytica (8.1%), with E. chattoni (5.95%), E. moshkovskii (0.79%), and E. nuttalli (0.6%) at lower frequencies. A 504-sample molecular survey using PCR and SSU rRNA sequencing distinguished six species; E. histolytica was detected in ~8% of samples (about 1 in 12). Phylogenetic analysis of 247 E. coli isolates revealed two genotypes, SZ E. coli CEMs1 and CEMs2, clustering within the major E. coli clade and showing close affinity to strains from humans and other primates, implying cross-species movement. An age effect increases E. coli infection risk (p<0.0001), suggesting accumulation with age. Findings underscore zoonotic transmission risk for facilities housing macaques near human caretakers, impacting animal welfare, biomedical research validity, and staff safety; routine molecular surveillance is advocated.

article.articleHeadline: Mycoplasma Coinfection Raises Odds of Severe Pneumonia in Children With
article.articleSummary: Jinan, China: a retrospective study of 1,611 hospitalized children aged birth to under 18 with human metapneumovirus lower respiratory tract infection (2023–2025) found Mycoplasma pneumoniae co-detection markedly raised severe pneumonia risk. Overall, 301 children (18.7%) developed severe pneumonia and 36 (2.2%) required ICU care; infants 0–6 months had the highest ICU rate at 7.9%. In children over six years, atelectasis occurred in 22.4%, unilateral involvement 65.7%, and severe pneumonia 31.0%. Multivariable analysis identified atelectasis as the strongest predictor (adjusted OR 47.52), followed by chronic disease (OR 9.49), radiological consolidation (OR 6.82), fever (OR 3.29), and wheeze (OR 2.50). Mycoplasma pneumoniae co-detection nearly doubled odds of severe pneumonia (aOR 1.90). Higher absolute neutrophil counts and CRP linked to severity; higher monocyte counts (aOR 0.71) and broad bacterial co-detection (aOR 0.60) associated with lower odds. Age was not a predictor, though M. pneumoniae co-detection rose with age to 50% in >6 years.

article.articleHeadline: Municipal Public Health Clinical Center Named National Center for Infectious Disease Medicine "Regional Demonstration Center for Rapid Initiation of Antiretroviral Therapy for HIV"
article.articleSummary: Municipal Public Health Clinical Center has been named a National Center for Infectious Disease Medicine Regional Demonstration Center for Rapid Initiation of Antiretroviral Therapy for HIV, one of 13 nationwide. Emphasizing the motto 'early detection, rapid start, early treatment,' the center advances standardized HIV care with a streamlined, one-stop pathway for screening, referral, diagnosis and treatment in collaboration with disease-control authorities. The designation centers on rapid ART initiation—on the day of diagnosis and within seven days—alongside guideline adherence and treatment success as core performance indicators, illustrating effective medical–epidemiologic collaboration and quality-control across the care continuum. The accolade marks a milestone in high-quality infectious diseases development. Future work includes expanding the regional model through infection and immunology clinics, strengthening CDC partnerships, refining workflows and quality standards, and promoting regional academic exchanges and technical support to elevate HIV care nationwide.

article.articleHeadline: Respiratory Syncytial Virus to Enter the Epidemic Season; the elderly and the very young are high-risk groups; antibiotic treatment is ineffective.
article.articleSummary: RSV enters its typical peak season (October–April). Beijing You’an Hospital infectious disease expert Li Tongzeng notes there is no specific antiviral; treatment is supportive. Young children, especially under one year, and older adults with COPD, diabetes, or immune compromise are high-risk for pneumonia and potentially respiratory failure. Early RSV symptoms resemble a common cold—nasal congestion, runny nose, mild cough and fever—but RSV can progress to lower respiratory tract infection with higher fever, wheeze, chest tightness, and, in infants, irritability or poor feeding. Most mild cases can be managed at home with rest, fluids, antipyretics, saline nasal irrigation, and humidification; nebulization may relieve symptoms. Severe cases require hospitalization with oxygen and respiratory support. A long-acting monoclonal antibody is approved in China for infants under six months or those with congenital heart disease or chronic lung disease to reduce infection and severe outcomes. Adults have low risk but can transmit to high-risk household members; emphasize ventilation, hand hygiene, and masking in enclosed spaces.

article.articleHeadline: 4 Cebu provincial hospitals prepare to offer TB infection blood tests
article.articleSummary: Four Cebu provincial hospitals—Capitol-run in Balamban, Bogo, Carcar, and Danao—prepare to offer Interferon-Gamma Release Assay (IGRA) blood tests for TB infection, in a WHO and DOH-7 Central Visayas collaboration. IGRA detects TB infection from a single blood draw, unlike skin tests that require follow-up visits; samples are sent to laboratories for analysis, and a positive result does not by itself indicate active TB. Those with positive results will undergo medical evaluation and may receive chest X-rays or sputum testing. The program targets high‑risk individuals and close household contacts to identify latent TB and guide preventive treatment. Cebu’s expansion follows WHO Philippines discussions to strengthen TB testing; the Philippines ranks third globally for TB burden (about 6.8% of world cases) with ~500 new cases per 100,000 people in 2024.

article.articleHeadline: Multiplex LAMP-LFA for rapid field-compatible detection of environmental DNA from Schistosoma japonicum and Oncomelania hupensis quadrasi
article.articleSummary: Multiplex LAMP-LFA enables simultaneous detection of Schistosoma japonicum and its intermediate host, Oncomelania hupensis quadrasi, in freshwater from Ekiran village, Alangalang, Leyte Province, Philippines. Field-adaptable assay using environmental DNA (eDNA) was evaluated at 30 sites across four surveys from July 2023 to March 2024. The mLAMP-LFA demonstrated limits of detection from 57.2 to 194.9 copies per reaction, with 95% CIs of 7.7-427.3 to 35.2-1,077.9 copies. No cross-reactivity with non-target species observed. Compared with traditional malacological surveys, detection of S. japonicum rose from 1.7% to 18.5%, and O. h. quadrasi from 10.9% to 15.1%. Agreement with reference methods (Gwet's AC1) was substantial for S. japonicum (0.774-0.779) and moderate-to-substantial for O. h. quadrasi (0.538-0.766), both p<0.001. The approach offers rapid, field-ready, equipment-minimal multiplex eDNA surveillance to strengthen schistosomiasis monitoring and targeted control in resource-limited endemic settings.

article.articleHeadline: Woman's brain worm infection confirmed after eggs grow tails in lab test
article.articleSummary: Philippines rice farmer presented with a one-minute seizure affecting the right side. MRI revealed a bright cluster of nodules with surrounding fluid in the left frontal lobe. A New England Journal of Medicine case report identified suspected neuroschistosomiasis from Schistosoma japonicum, found in the Philippines, China, and parts of Indonesia. S. japonicum eggs typically shed in urine or feces; on rare occasions eggs reach the central nervous system and lodge in the brain, causing seizures. Diagnosis was supported by circumoval precipitin testing, which produced tail-like antibody bindings on the eggs, and stool testing showing 190 eggs per gram. Final diagnosis: cerebral schistosomiasis with focal seizure. Treatment included an antiparasitic, an anti-inflammatory, and an antiseizure medication. After three months, seizures abated and follow-up MRI showed disappearance of eggs.

article.articleHeadline: Seafood contaminated with poisonous crabs could trigger a major disaster; during crab season, beware these marine "toxins"
article.articleSummary: Published 2026-09-23. Seafood contaminated with poisonous crabs could trigger a major disaster during crab season. A market incident where a small crab mixed with squid was identified as a red-spotted crab carrying tetrodotoxin; even tiny amounts can be fatal, and high-heat cooking does not destroy the toxin. The article lists dangerous marine organisms and regions: red-spotted crab and copper-crusted crab (both with tetrodotoxin) found around Japan, the Philippines, Singapore, and China’s Guangdong and Hainan; textile cone snail and blue-ringed octopus with tetrodotoxin; box jellyfish with severe venom. Spoiled shrimp and crabs can harbor Vibrio parahaemolyticus, reaching pathogenic levels within six hours at 35°C. Prevention tips: avoid unfamiliar seafood, buy from reputable markets, keep raw and cooked seafood separate, and cook to 100°C. Vulnerable groups should avoid raw or undercooked seafood. Three rules: don’t eat unfamiliar, don’t buy unfamiliar, don’t handle unfamiliar seafood.

article.articleHeadline: Influenza A Begins to Draw Attention, DKI Jakarta Health Office: No Significant Surge Yet in Jakarta.
article.articleSummary: Influenza A draws attention in Indonesia as Jakarta reports no significant surge. Health authorities urge the public to stay calm and follow proper hygiene: clean hands with soap, mask when ill or in crowded places, cough etiquette, adequate nutrition, fluids, and rest. Separately, WHO Western Pacific Region data as of 10 September 2026 show Southeast Asian countries with higher influenza positivity: Singapore 24–37%, Brunei 28%, Malaysia 19–20%, Vietnam 7–20%, while Indonesia has not observed a worrying surge, per MoH.

triage.headline_ja: インフルエンザAが注目を集め始める、ジャカルタ特別州保健局：ジャカルタでは顕著な急増はまだ見られず
triage.triage_reason: 季節性インフルエンザの地域的な陽性率上昇が報告されているが、ジャカルタでは明確な急増は確認されておらず、重大な公衆衛生上の懸念には至っていない。周辺国の動向を含め継続的な監視が必要。
triage.notes: 記事はインドネシア（ジャカルタ）における状況が主題であり、ISPA症例の増加は季節性パターンと整合的でインフルエンザA自体の急増は確認されていない。シンガポール・ブルネイ・マレーシア・ベトナムの陽性率データは参考情報として言及されているが、これらの国は対象国リストにベトナム以外含まれず、ベトナムについても記事の主題ではないため verified_locations には含めない。

article.articleHeadline: 60,000 chickens and ducks collapse and die after floods; a farm owner in Thanh Hoa suffers 7 billion dong in losses.
article.articleSummary: Around 60,000 chickens and ducks died at Ho Mo Xanh poultry farm in Nong Cong Commune, Thanh Hoa Province, after mid-September floods, with estimated losses of VND 7 billion. By 22 September, workers were removing carcasses, clearing mud, and moving surviving birds to higher ground to prevent further losses. Floodwaters damaged the farm’s ventilation and cooling systems, causing heat stress and mass mortality. Carcasses are being bagged, buried with lime, and the site will be cleaned with brooms and high-pressure water, followed by disinfection to curb disease risk. Surviving birds are separated and monitored with continued water and feed. Local authorities in Nong Cong are promoting environmental hygiene and disease prevention as recovery begins in stages. The article notes ongoing risk of disease after floods, but no specific pathogen laboratory confirmation is reported.

triage.headline_ja: 洪水後に6万羽の鶏・アヒルが死亡、タインホア省の農場主が70億ドンの損失
triage.triage_reason: 家禽の大量死は洪水による換気・冷却設備の損傷とそれに伴う熱ストレスが原因であり、感染症の病原体は確認されていない。公衆衛生上の懸念は低い。
triage.notes: 死因は洪水による設備損傷・熱ストレスであり、感染症病原体の検査確認は報告されていない。今後の疾病リスクについて地元当局が予防的措置を講じているが、現時点で感染症シグナルとしての根拠は乏しい。

article.articleHeadline: Looking for a person bitten by a dog.
article.articleSummary: Urgent social-media post sought a man bitten by a dog that had died, suspected rabies; the victim, a Gia Lai plant seller, was found and by Sept 14 had begun rabies vaccination. The episode shows how social-media reach can influence rabies risk timing and highlights free-roaming dogs in Vietnamese cities and dog waste in public spaces. Fines exist for not muzzling, vaccinating, or allowing defecation, but enforcement is weak due to limited inspectors, reluctance to confront neighbors, and cumbersome procedures. Global best practices rely on mandatory animal identification via microchips (Singapore, EU), dog ownership taxes (Germany), and licensing/tests (Hundeführerschein) in parts of Germany and Switzerland, plus compulsory civil liability insurance. Vietnam should adopt a data-driven system: a digitized pet database linked to owner's citizen ID, expanded chip services at communes, and rapid penalties via camera surveillance.

triage.headline_ja: 犬に噛まれた人物を捜索
triage.triage_reason: 個別の狂犬病曝露事例であり、被害者は特定されワクチン接種を開始済み。公衆衛生上の深刻な拡大リスクや異常性は認められず、記事の主眼はペット管理制度に関する政策論評である。
triage.notes: 記事はベトナムの個別狂犬病曝露事例を発端に、動物管理・犬の登録制度に関する政策提言を行う内容。シンガポール・ドイツ・スイスは比較事例として言及されているのみで実際の発生国ではない。

article.articleHeadline: Two African Swine Fever Outbreaks Detected in Mai Phụ Commune, Urgent Response Underway
article.articleSummary: Two African Swine Fever outbreaks were detected in Mai Phụ Commune, Hà Tĩnh Province, Vietnam, with pig deaths in two households. On September 8, Lê Văn Tĩnh’s Gia Mỹ hamlet reported 5 pigs dead (232 kg total) and on September 20, Nguyễn Văn Đàn’s Ngọc Mỹ hamlet reported 4 pigs dead (216 kg). Laboratory confirmation by the National Center for Veterinary Diagnostics and Testing I linked the deaths to ASF. Mai Phụ has about 550 pig-raising households and roughly 2,700 pigs. Local authorities have enacted containment measures: rapid herd surveillance, mandatory reporting of unexplained illness or death, and prohibitions on raising or restocking during the outbreak in Gia Mỹ and Ngọc Mỹ. Disinfection with lime and chemicals is required; slaughter must occur at licensed facilities; movement and sale of pigs and products are strictly controlled with penalties for violations. Officials are coordinating response and funding for compensation.

triage.headline_ja: マイフー社にて豚コレラ（アフリカ豚熱）2件発生、緊急対応進行中
triage.triage_reason: 動物疾病（アフリカ豚熱）であり、ヒトへの公衆衛生上の影響は報告されておらず、国際的拡大や渡航・貿易制限のリスクも記事からは確認できない。
triage.notes: アフリカ豚熱は豚のみに感染し、ヒトに感染しないため公衆衛生上の懸念は低い。地元当局による家畜疾病対応（隔離・消毒・移動制限）が実施されている。

article.articleHeadline: Soomaaliya oo xoojisay diyaar-garowga Ebola iyadoo Muqdisho lagu qabtay tababar xaalad-degdeg ah
article.articleSummary: Ebola preparedness training in Mogadishu, Somalia, completed by the Ministry of Health and Social Care and the National Institute of Public Health with WHO support. No Ebola cases in Somalia to date. About 70 participants from the federal Ministry, the National Institute, regional authorities, and partners tested capacity to detect, verify, report, and respond to an imported Ebola event. The exercise evaluated interagency coordination, entry screening, patient referral, data sharing, and community awareness, plus emergency-response planning. Six simulated scenarios covered regional health alerts, crowd movement, a suspected Ebola case at entry points, unverified reports, and leadership decisions. Gaps were identified in reporting, notification, port-of-entry procedures, media roles, and next steps, with a follow-up plan. As of 7 September 2026, Congo reports 6,757 confirmed cases and 3,267 deaths across 61 health facilities in six regions. All simulations; no actual patient, specimen, or Ebola case was involved.

triage.headline_ja: ソマリアがエボラ対応準備を強化、モガディシュで緊急事態対応訓練を実施
triage.triage_reason: 本記事はソマリアにおけるエボラ対応の模擬訓練（演習）に関する報告であり、実際の症例発生はない。DRCの流行状況は既知の背景情報として言及されているのみで、新規シグナルとは言えない。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はソマリアでの訓練演習（実患者・検体は関与せず）。DRCのエボラ流行データ（6,757例、3,267死亡）は既知の継続流行の現状報告として引用されているのみで、本記事の主題ではないため verified_locations には含めない。ソマリアは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: G20+ meeting on Wednesday in New York to accelerate collective action against Ebola - ACP.
article.articleSummary: G20+ foreign ministers meeting to accelerate action against Ebola will be held September 23, 2026, in New York, United States, on the margins of the United Nations General Assembly. Africa CDC welcomes U.S. leadership and notes participation by the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda, aiming to link international commitments with national priorities and the needs of affected communities and frontline responders. The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo remains the focus of discussions as the health crisis enters its fifth month and is framed as a global security issue. The event underscores diplomatic and health coordination in the ongoing response to this Ebola crisis.

triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で継続中のエボラ流行（発生5ヶ月目）が国際的な外交・保健協調の焦点となっており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するため。
triage.notes: 記事自体はG20+外相会議の開催告知が主題だが、背景にあるDRCのエボラ流行（5ヶ月継続、国際安全保障課題として位置づけ）が実質的なイベントであるためPICKUPと判断。ウガンダ・米国は会議参加国として言及されているが、エボラ発生国ではないためverified_locationsから除外。

article.articleHeadline: The DRC temporarily suspends the export of its primates due to the Ebola outbreak.
article.articleSummary: Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) temporarily suspends CITES export permits for primates due to an Ebola outbreak with the Bundibugyo variant raging in the DRC since May 2026. A letter from ICCN Director-General Yves Milan Ngangay (Aug 28, 2026) invokes the precautionary principle to halt primate exports to protect species with high mortality if infected, per the World Organisation for Animal Health. Bonobo habituation expert Félix Bofeko, based at Salonga National Park in the north, says the move supports in situ conservation and reduces cross-species transmission. American ecologist Julie Sherman of Wildlife Impact notes the risk to both great apes and humans from close contact in the trade. The suspension also stops trade with Indian firm Vantara, a major buyer, amid concerns about animal origins, permit issuance, and data used to justify exports. Conservationists largely welcome the measure amid ongoing trafficking pressures on hundreds of primates in the DRC.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国、エボラ流行を理由に霊長類の輸出を一時停止
triage.triage_reason: DRCで2026年5月から続くエボラ（ブンディブギョ株）流行を理由に、CITES輸出許可が一時停止されるなど公衆衛生・貿易制限措置が取られており、IHR基準で複数該当するため。
triage.notes: 記事は主にコンゴ民主共和国での霊長類輸出停止措置に焦点を当てており、米国・インドは輸出先/取引企業の文脈で言及されているのみで、実際の感染症発生地域ではないため除外した。

article.articleHeadline: Tanzania sets 2040 target to eradicate sheep, goat disease - Daily News
article.articleSummary: Peste des Petits Ruminants (PPR), a highly contagious viral disease of sheep and goats, is Tanzania’s priority for eradication by 2040, extending the initial 2030 target. As of 22 September 2026, the drive ties livestock health to household livelihoods, especially for women and youth, and regional livestock trade. A five-year national vaccination and identification campaign has secured more than 216 billion shillings, with over 16 million goats and sheep vaccinated in the first year and more than 50 million livestock vaccinated during the first phase; more than 30 billion shillings is allocated for the current financial year to support the second phase. Emphasis on sustained surveillance, risk-based vaccination, and cross-border cooperation with Angola and the Democratic Republic of the Congo aims to curb transmission. The Regional PPR Buffer Ecosystems Workshop in Dar es Salaam (Sept 14–16) underscored shared border risks and information sharing, with AU-IBAR recognizing President Samia’s contributions.

triage.headline_ja: タンザニア、羊・ヤギの疾病撲滅目標を2040年に設定
triage.triage_reason: 小反芻獣疫（PPR）は家畜（羊・ヤギ）のみに感染するウイルス性疾患であり、ヒトへの健康被害はなく、内容もタンザニア政府のワクチン接種・撲滅プログラムに関する行政発表である。
triage.notes: PPRは家畜伝染病でヒト感染症ではない。DRC・アンゴラは国境を越えた協力関係の文脈で言及されているのみで、実際の発生国ではない。タンザニアは対象国リストに含まれないため、verified_locationsは空配列とした。

article.articleHeadline: The Chinese Embassy in the Democratic Republic of the Congo reminds Chinese citizens in the DRC to take precautions against the risk of an Ebola outbreak.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has spread to Bas-Uele, Tshopo/Tshopo, and South Ubangi provinces. In Bas-Uele, health zones affected are Buta, Ganga, and Viadana; in Tshopo/Tshopo, Makiso-Kisangani, Mangobo, Lubunga, Bafwasende, Kabondo, Wani-Rukula, and Tshopo; in South Ubangi, Bulu. Kisangani, located in Tshopo, is a major transport hub, raising transmission and importation risks. The Chinese Embassy in Kinshasa urges Chinese nationals and corporations to monitor the outbreak and local containment measures, and to avoid travel to the three provinces. Guidance emphasizes avoiding contact with confirmed or suspected cases and their materials, strict hygiene, avoiding wild animal contact and unknown meat, and seeking prompt medical care if fever or bleeding symptoms appear. Evacuation plans require 21 days of health monitoring; contact embassy and local health authorities for emergencies. Emergency contacts: WHO Africa Regional Office +47-24139402; Chinese consular/hotline +86-10-12308, +86-10-65612308; embassy protection +243-851474669.

triage.headline_ja: 在コンゴ民主共和国中国大使館、エボラ出血熱アウトブレイクのリスクに対する予防措置を在留中国人に呼びかけ
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で複数州にエボラ出血熱の感染が拡大しており、主要交通拠点キサンガニを含む地域での感染・拡散リスクが高いため、フルリスク評価が必要と判断。

article.articleHeadline: The Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda bring Ebola diagnosis closer to border communities
article.articleSummary: DRC and Uganda deploy a mobile Ebola diagnostic laboratory in Kasenyi, Ituri Province, near the Lake Albert border crossing with Uganda, to accelerate confirmation of Bundibugyo virus disease in the Tchomia health zone (population >94,000). Before 23 July 2026, Kasenyi samples were transported 55 km to Bunia with poor roads, delaying results up to five hours. Since deployment, analyses are conducted on-site and results are available in about one hour, enabling faster isolation and cross-border surveillance. The mobile unit was installed after confirmed Bundibugyo virus disease cases and is operated by a nine-member Congolese laboratory team alongside Ugandan counterparts; Rebecca Mave handles sample reception, decontamination and preparation under strict biosafety protocols. Supported by WHO and partners, the collaboration aims to interrupt transmission by cross-border information sharing and coordinated interventions, recognizing that viruses do not recognize borders.

article.articleHeadline: Social media spread unverified information about Ebola, doctors warn.
article.articleSummary: On 2026-09-22, doctors in Ho Chi Minh City warn about unverified Ebola information on social media and urge calm. The HCMC Center for Disease Control (HCDC) hosted a forum to share scientific facts and prevention. Ebola is an acute viral hemorrhagic fever with case fatality rates from 25% to 90%, averaging about 50%. It is not airborne; transmission occurs by direct contact with blood or body fluids of an infected person or animal, or contaminated objects; spillover from wildlife can occur. Symptomatic individuals are contagious, incubation is not. As of 20-9, WHO reports 7,672 confirmed cases in the Democratic Republic of Congo, 3,699 related deaths, and 886 in treatment. Ho Chi Minh City maintains 24/7 border quarantine at Tan Son Nhat Airport and seaports to detect and refer suspected cases. Travelers to Africa should limit contact with the sick and seek care on return. France reports the first imported Ebola case, a doctor returning from Congo.

triage.triage_reason: DRCで大規模エボラ流行が継続（7,672症例、3,699死亡）しており、フランスへの輸入症例も発生。国際的拡大とIHR基準の複数該当が認められる。

article.articleHeadline: Kisangani: Women briefed on Ebola prevention and rumor management - ACP
article.articleSummary: Sept 22, 2026, Kisangani, the capital of Tshopo in the Democratic Republic of Congo, hosted a briefing for women from feminist associations and civil-society groups on Ebola virus disease (EVD). Dr. Christian Tshilenge outlined EVD definition, symptoms, prevention methods, and actions to take if infection is suspected, with an emphasis on countering circulating rumors amid an infodemic in Tshopo. The goal was to strengthen participants’ ability to provide reliable information and to relay persistent rumors to response teams for clarification. After the session, the women will act as community relays, sharing knowledge within their associations and networks. Organized by the Provincial Health Division, the activity supports risk communication and community engagement to raise awareness and curb misinformation in the Ebola response.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola in Kisangani: Frontline Health Workers Urged to Bolster Their Protection Through Vaccination - ACP
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease (EVD) is currently circulating in Kisangani, the capital of Tshopo Province in northeastern Democratic Republic of Congo. Frontline health workers are being vaccinated as a key protective measure, following the vaccination of acting governor Didier Lomoyo and his team in the Makiso-Kisangani health zone. Dr. Maurice Kongot, zone medical chief, stressed that officials who interact with the public are at similar risk and should receive the vaccine to stay protected. The vice-governor’s vaccination also serves as a public signal, encouraging colleagues to follow suit. To counter lingering doubts, health authorities urged the population to heed ongoing outreach messages and take the epidemic seriously. The official noted that this is the 17th Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo, and that Ebola has been present in the country since 1976, a real health threat rather than a myth.

article.articleHeadline: DRC: In Kinshasa, WHO bets on female leadership to strengthen the polio response.
article.articleSummary: In Kinshasa, the World Health Organization organized a September 21 workshop to strengthen gender equality and female leadership within the Democratic Republic of the Congo's polio eradication programme. The meeting brought polio programme stakeholders to advance gender equity, professional development, and leadership skills, with the goal of increasing women's representation in managerial roles and fostering a supportive network for career progression. A six-month mentoring program will accompany participants after training, building a talent pool and facilitating cross-practice exchanges among professionals, demonstrating that women have the capacity to assume greater leadership in the response. The workshop also aims to integrate gender, equity, and human rights principles into vaccination, surveillance, and outbreak response. Dr Landoh Essoya Dadja, Incident Manager for polio at the WHO DRC office, attended, underscoring the commitment to a stronger, more durable polio programme via female leadership.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola: NCDC introduces new measures for travellers into Nigeria
article.articleSummary: Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) measures announced by Nigeria’s NCDC in response to the ongoing outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). Travellers from countries with active or relevant EVD transmission may be required to complete Health Declaration Forms to support surveillance, risk assessment, contact follow-up, and early detection; travellers from other countries are temporarily exempt, reflecting a risk-based approach. The advisory follows consultations with public health experts and the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, aiming to keep Nigeria's preparedness proportionate to identified risks. The public is urged to stay vigilant for Ebola symptoms and seek medical attention if exposed or symptomatic; individuals with travel or exposure history should provide accurate information to healthcare workers. Preparatory activities are ongoing and measures will be updated as epidemiological information evolves, with coordination among the Federal Ministry of Health, Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria, Port Health Services, NIS, and NCAA, and support from WHO and Africa CDC.

triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で進行中のエボラ出血熱アウトブレイクに対し、ナイジェリアが渡航者向け水際対策を導入するなど、国際的拡大リスクと渡航制限措置が既に発生しているため、IHR基準を複数満たす。

article.articleHeadline: Opinion | Change in the epidemiology of meningitis reinforces the need to reassess prevention in Brazil.
article.articleSummary: Brazil faces meningococcal meningitis as a rapid, grave public health threat, with case fatality around 20%—twice the global rate—and infants under one year bearing the highest incidence (12.28 per 100,000). Early symptoms mimic other illnesses (fever, vomiting, headache, photophobia) and the disease can progress to severe forms and death within 24 hours. Serogroup C declined after vaccines (2010) and ACWY expansion (2020), shifting dominance to serogroup B; SBP data show B caused 73% of cases in infants <1 year in 2025 and 80% under 15. Outbreaks occurred in Maceió, Alagoas, and Belém, Pará. Meningococcal B vaccine is recommended by SBIm for 3, 5, and 12 months and is available in private networks; SBP estimates about two in three infant cases could be prevented with B vaccination. This epidemiological shift calls for updated prevention strategies in Brazil.

As a preventive measure, the Ministry authorized a 'dose zero' measles vaccine for children 6 months to 11 months 29 days in the three municipalities; dose zero does not replace the regular schedule. Authorities urge parents to check vaccination status and update vaccines. Symptoms: fever, red rash, cough, runny nose, conjunctivitis.

article.articleHeadline: Yellow fever vaccination that blocked Ronaldinho's entourage; in which countries is it mandatory?
article.articleSummary: Yellow fever vaccination certificates were required for Ronaldinho’s six-member entourage entering Kochi for the Return of the Titans after two travelers lacked a certificate; they later downloaded a digital vaccine card and submitted it. Travel from yellow fever–affected areas mandates a health card. The Americas show transmission in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela, with Colombia reporting the most cases; Brazil’s outbreak reemerged after decades, including 2017 when over 2,000 were infected and more than 700 died. CDC issued a Level 2 alert for Colombia, with Tolima reporting additional cases. Yellow fever is transmitted by Aedes, Haemagogus, and Sabethes mosquitoes; early symptoms include fever, headache, and myalgia, with about 15% progressing to severe disease and roughly 50% mortality in that stage. No antiviral exists; vaccination provides lifelong protection, with immunity developing in 10 days for 80–100% and over 99% by 30 days. Certificates are required by many countries for travelers from endemic areas, with strict enforcement in some transit-stop countries.

article.articleHeadline: Salmonella outbreak in eggs exposes a challenge for poultry farming
article.articleSummary: Salmonella Enteritidis outbreak linked to eggs in Belgium has sickened at least 306 people by August 2026, with a Geel, Flanders farm identified as the source and up to 2 million eggs potentially contaminated distributed across Europe. The episode highlights a poultry-farming challenge: infected birds may appear healthy, so clinical signs are unreliable. Salmonella can contaminate eggs during formation, reaching the reproductive tract and contaminating eggs before shelling. Control relies on ongoing monitoring, laboratory testing, and strict biosafety measures in production. In Brazil, the National Poultry Health Program (PNSA) includes Salmonella under official control; SDA Instruction No. 20 (2016) sets procedures for monitoring in certain commercial poultry establishments and federally inspected abattoirs. Rapid traceability and batch-level investigations are crucial to block affected products and reduce consumer exposure.

article.articleHeadline: Cryptosporidiosis in heifers: a study finds nearly fivefold difference in diarrhea risk between treatments.
article.articleSummary: Cryptosporidiosis in calves in Descalvado, São Paulo, Brazil, was investigated in 70 Holstein heifers naturally exposed to Cryptosporidium parvum. Forty calves received paromomycin (Parofor® Solution Oral) and 30 were treated with halofuginone, for seven days from day 5 to 11 of life. Halofuginone-treated calves had a 4.93-fold higher odds of diarrhea than those given paromomycin; they also experienced 3.4 times more days with diarrhea and 1.93 times more days requiring supportive therapy. Diarrhea incidence remained near zero up to day 10 in the paromomycin group, while it exceeded 60% between days 10 and 11 in the halofuginone group. By day 14, paromomycin calves weighed more, after equal starting weights at day 5 (42.9 kg). Fecal oocyst excretion was more variable and higher in halofuginone-treated calves, whereas paromomycin yielded steadier, lower excretion. Brazil-wide, Cryptosporidium spp prevalence in cattle is estimated around 30.5%.

article.articleHeadline: Measles Returns to the Americas, and Elimination Metrics May Need an
article.articleSummary: Americas lost measles-free regional verification on 10 November 2025 after the Regional Monitoring and Re-Verification Commission found endemic transmission reestablished in Canada; the rest of the hemisphere retained national elimination status, creating a mosaic of verified countries within an unverified region. A New Microbes and New Infections letter argues for two prospective indicators to supplement elimination status. In Brazil, São Paulo reported 23 measles cases from January to August 2026 (vs 2 in 2025), clustered in the capital and near the major international air hub corridor (Guarulhos; São Bernardo do Campo). The first two cases were imported; the remainder were import-related with sources unidentified. Brazil had reverificated as measles-free in November 2024, with endemic interruption since June 2022. The two proposed indicators: importation pressure—rolling three months, arriving passengers, incidence per million, and age-stratified, two-dose susceptibility—and surveillance traceability—the proportion of confirmed cases with no identifiable epidemiological link, reflecting investigation and linkage capacity.

article.articleHeadline: Dengue cases in Foz do Iguaçu fall from 209 to 28 in the second quadrimester.
article.articleSummary: Dengue in Foz do Iguaçu, Brazil, fell to 28 cases in the second quadrimester of 2026 from 209 in the same period in 2025, with no dengue deaths reported in 2025 or 2026. The Municipal Health Secretariat attributes the decline to continued vector-control and surveillance, including the second phase of the Wolbachia release and intensified environmental health education reaching 9,683 students across all grades. Family Health Strategy coverage now reaches 100% of the population, and September work hours increased from 30 to 36 per week, with absenteeism down from 13% to 10%. Officials emphasize cross-border collaboration with Paraguay and Argentina, planning an agenda in Asunción to discuss border health services and related cooperation with state and federal authorities. The report highlights integrated action and ongoing capacity-building within municipal health programs.

article.articleHeadline: Endophytic Fungus Transforms Tree Diterpene Into Potent Antiparasitic
article.articleSummary: Brazilian researchers report that endophytic fungus Aspergillus sclerotiorum, isolated from leaves of Mexican cypress Cupressus lusitanica, selectively oxidizes ent-pimara-8(14),15-dien-19-oic acid by epoxidizing the vinyl group while preserving the internal double bond. The biotransformation yields four products; two are known (15,16-epoxy-ent-pimar-8(14)-en-19-oic acid; 15,16-dihydroxy-ent-pimar-8(14)-en-19-oic acid) and two are novel (17-hydroxy-15,16-epoxy-ent-pimar-8(14)-en-19-oic acid; 15-oxo-16-hydroxy-ent-pimar-8(14)-en-19-oic acid). One of the new diterpenes shows strong activity against parasites causing leishmaniasis and Chagas disease. The study highlights unusual regioselectivity compared with prior microbes; structures elucidated by NMR and HRMS, and genome mining identified two cytochrome P450 candidates. Docking suggests the vinyl group and C-13 methyl reside near the heme center, guiding oxidation, revealing a potentially new enzymatic route to antiparasitic diterpenes (International Microbiology, 2026-09-22).

The facility results from a public-private partnership between the Brazilian government, Tecpar, and Biogénesis Bagó. Brazil has been recognized since 2024 as FMD-free without vaccination, but maintains vigilant surveillance to prevent reintroduction and protect beef exports. When a disease focus is detected, the antigen is thawed, vaccine formulated within four days, and supplies can be deployed to the outbreak site within seven days. The bank does not hold ready-to-use vaccines; it provides materials to produce them. Challenges include rapid viral characterization and ensuring availability of supplies and packaging to enable fast response and minimize trade disruption.

article.articleHeadline: Brazilian Agroforests Harbor Surprising Mosquito Diversity and Disease
article.articleSummary: Three-year study (2022–2025) at Terra Boa Farm, Silva Jardim, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil documented 5,314 immature mosquitoes from 38 species. Culex dominated (53.8%), followed by Limatus (16.6%) and Wyeomyia (16.2%); five species—Cx. iridescens, Cx. pleuristriatus, Lim. durhamii, Wy. edwardsi, and Ae. albopictus—made up about 80% of captures. Natural habitats (bromeliads, bamboo internodes, peach palm bracts) yielded 4,175 specimens (78.6%) and 34 species, with 26 exclusive to natural sites; bromeliads produced 2,031 individuals from 22 species. Bamboo internodes were dominated by Cx. iridescens (72.4%) and harbored Toxorhynchites trichopygus larvae. Artificial containers (tarps and a 200-L barrel) held 1,139 specimens from 12 species, led by Li. durhamii and Ae. albopictus (tarps 83.7%). Cx. quinquefasciatus appeared in tarps; sylvatic yellow fever vectors Haemagogus leucocelaenus/janthinomys and Sabethes identicus were found in bamboo near Poço das Antas reserve, signaling spillover risk and the ecological plasticity of vectors in agroforestry, with Ae. albopictus as a generalist.

article.articleHeadline: Invasive Asian Malaria Mosquito Proves as Susceptible to African Parasites
article.articleSummary: Anopheles stephensi, the invasive Asian malaria mosquito spreading across the Horn of Africa since Djibouti’s 2012 detection, shows similar susceptibility to Plasmodium falciparum as the native An. arabiensis. In Metehara, central Ethiopia, researchers performed paired direct membrane feeding assays with blood from 43 patients carrying P. falciparum gametocytes (Aug 2024–Jan 2025). Mosquitoes from Adama’s colony—An. stephensi (25th generation) and An. arabiensis—fed in parallel on the same patient blood. Feeding efficiency: 78.3% stephensi vs 85% arabiensis; infection of at least one mosquito: 68–70% in both; oocyst carriage: 30.7% for both species. Oocyst counts averaged ~20,000 (stephensi) vs ~28,000 (arabiensis) with median densities of 13.5 vs 26.3. The strong correlation (0.85) suggests urban An. stephensi can sustain African P. falciparum transmission, informing malaria-control efforts amid the vector’s wider spread from Djibouti to Ethiopia, Sudan, Somalia, Nigeria, Yemen, Kenya, Ghana, and Niger.

article.articleHeadline: Zambia : Mwansabombwe Urged To Heighten Disease Preparedness
article.articleSummary: Cholera preparedness strengthened in Mwansabombwe District, Zambia, as Acting District Commissioner Katele Lengwe urged the District Epidemic Preparedness Committee to stay vigilant after cholera outbreaks were reported in other parts of the country. Lengwe stressed that epidemic preparedness requires multi‑sector collaboration across government departments, the local authority, health facilities, traditional and civic leaders, cooperating partners, communities and other stakeholders. The warning comes as two cholera cases were reported in neighbouring Chiengi District. Council Secretary Felix Mwila noted Mwansabombwe has not recorded a cholera outbreak in the past three years and called for joint action to address water supply, hygiene and sanitation to prevent outbreaks. The report does not provide details on symptoms, laboratory confirmation, infection source, or any imported/exported cases.

article.articleHeadline: SYPHILIS FIGHT TAKEN INTO COMMUNITIES - Zambia 24
article.articleSummary: Zambia on 22 September 2026 launched the Stop Syphilis Campaign in Lusaka in partnership with the AIDS Healthcare Foundation (AHF) to curb rising syphilis and other sexually transmitted infections. The Ministry of Health emphasised community-based interventions beyond hospital settings, urging testing and treatment uptake across communities, including antenatal clinics and outreach programs. Health officials highlighted that syphilis remains curable but serious, with particular concern for ages 15–49 and pregnant women, where untreated infection risks miscarriages, stillbirths and congenital syphilis. The campaign will include condom distribution, expanded testing kits and treatment supplies, enhanced health worker training, and real-time data monitoring. Partners will support integrated screening, broader STI prevention messaging, and sustained resources beyond the launch. Dr Lisulo Walubuta stressed reducing barriers to testing; Dr Webster Chewe warned of silent transmission and congenital risks.
